quest.title: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence
quest.description: You learned in the tavern that the alarm at Dornman Port's old lighthouse seems to be malfunctioning. Rumors say that it's caused by ghosts beneath the lighthouse...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: You wouldn't know, Odolf. The Knights have already been there more times than I can count...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Well, I've been in Snezhnaya lately. This is actually the first I've heard that the Knights have all been to the lighthouse... So what happened?

dialogues.speaker: Lennart
dialogues.text: What do you think? The alarm in the old lighthouse still flickers from time to time. At first, Winslow would shout, "The Abyss! It's the Abyss!"

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: The Knights took him seriously and went in fully armed, only to find there wasn't a single trace of the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: After running back and forth like that a few times, they were completely worn out.

dialogues.speaker: Lennart
dialogues.text: If you ask me, it's just the old alarm mechanisms beneath the lighthouse wearing down. But... Well... there have been some rumors lately...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Oh, goodness. And what kind of rumors could that be?

dialogues.speaker: Lennart
dialogues.text: Rumors that the ghosts of knights, fallen in battle long ago, are the ones still seen wandering there...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: G—Ghosts!

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: Whoa, you two. Don't yell when you're talking about scary things. You guys are even scarier than ghosts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: S—Sorry, Paimon didn't mean to...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: It's alright, it's alright. Conversations are always livelier with more people. And you are...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You introduce yourselves to the group at the table...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon... Oh, I see...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: By the way, how is Winslow doing these days?

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: He was terrified by the light from the alarm. Living in the old lighthouse with mechanisms going off all the time would drive anyone crazy.

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: I've heard he's been acting a little crazy lately... Then again, you could say that's his well-deserved punishment. Why do you even care about him?

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Well, we can't just leave the alarm mechanism as it is. As a matter of fact, I live near the old lighthouse. And besides...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: There might be something else down there. I won't be able to rest easy until we go and check it out. We can't just leave poor old Winslow stuck there either, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... If that's the case, then the thing we ran into outside the old lighthouse earlier...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Hm? You two ran into something near the old lighthouse? My oh my, could it be a ghost?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No. We met someone who looked frantic and completely out of it. Probably the person living in the old lighthouse, right?

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: ...Winslow.

response.speaker: Lennart
response.text: You want to help Winslow?

response.speaker: Lennart
response.text: Just so we're clear, the area below used to be an ancient battlefield. I'm not risking my life down there. Besides, even the Knights of Favonius have checked it out, and the problem still hasn't been solved...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: That means we'll need someone even more reliable than the Knights. Say, a great hero who saved Mondstadt in the past, for example...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph hmph~ And where exactly could anyone find a hero like that?

choices.text: Look no further... for the great hero is standing right here!

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Haha, brave heroes, forgive my bluntness, but might you possibly entertain my humble request for help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Emm... But there are those annoying ghosts...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Ah, but some stories say ghosts linger only to guard treasures hidden deep in the mountains...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! Treasure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #It's not about the treasure, {NICKNAME}. That person living in the old lighthouse sounds really miserable.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Okay, okay...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: I knew you two wouldn't refuse. Ah, even if there were no treasure at all, I'd still be more than happy to offer some compensation for this adventure.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: #...In fact, I should make some preparations myself. {NICKNAME}, how about we meet later at the foot of the old lighthouse?

response.speaker: Lennart
response.text: This sounds like too much trouble. I'm staying out of it. I've had too much to drink and need to lie down.

response.speaker: Matthew
response.text: #Go home and get some proper rest, Lennart. *sigh* Best of luck to you all. And Odolf, even with {NICKNAME} around, don't do anything reckless.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Of course.

choices.text: Paimon takes the bait so easily...
Oh no, they're coming for our heads!

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Well, you do happen to be here... And you know what they say, there is no greater beauty to be found in this world than that of verse and chance. To be honest, even if you're not here, I was planning to investigate on my own anyway.

choices.text: Yeah, the one that looked suspicious...

talks.objective: Head to the base of the old lighthouse

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Odolf!

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. You arrived even sooner than I expected...

choices.text: You still need more time to prepare?

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: No. Everything that needed doing is already done... Ah, what I said just now wasn't a complaint. It was a compliment.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Punctuality is rare. Most only keep others waiting... Sometimes, arriving early is a virtue in itself.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Hmm... take a look. This is the kind of mechanism that's been sounding the alarm. It activates because...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a ghost! Right here, right now!

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Oh my. Looks like there's a ghost among the three of us, then. I can assure you I'm a living person. I was drinking beer just now.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm a living person too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, the ghost is Paimon... That's not right!

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Haha. It would appear that there are no ghosts among us. In that case, the alarm probably wasn't triggered by a ghost.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: I think it could be the abnormal airflow. Old-fashioned mechanisms like this tend to grow overly sensitive. Even the slightest movement can set them off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Odolf knows so much about this mechanism.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Ah... well, I am a local. It's only natural that locals know a few secrets outsiders don't.

choices.text: Yeah, a local. That explains it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...You didn't understand a word of that, did you?

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Haha. That's not important, my friends.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: The mechanism itself is just overly sensitive. The real issue is the wind that shouldn't be blowing out from the underground ruins...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Wind coming up from underground... That does sound unsettling when I put it that way. In any case, we won't know the exact cause until we go down there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But the door is closed right now...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: <color=#00E1FFFF>These doors are all connected to the alarm.</color> Since the alarm is malfunctioning, the doors are broken too... Or perhaps Winslow did something.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: ...I heard he shut every door he could, trying to block out... whatever it was. In the end, he just locked out the kindhearted people like us.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: The only thing that can keep out all evils is an open heart and a clear conscience.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: ...But no matter. I know another route, one only us locals know. Let's head down that way.

choices.text: Alarm mechanisms are considered local customs now?

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: If an alarm mechanism has been around for a long time, it eventually becomes part of local customs and traditions. Just like the windmills in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Anyway, that's not the point.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: Haha, no, that's not what I meant. Sorry, I should have chosen my words more wisely.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: It's a good thing you arrived early. For example... it means we can start the investigation sooner.

talks.objective: Go to the other entrance to the ruins at the base of the lighthouse

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: This is strange. Odolf is being unusually eager this time. Wasn't there some bad blood between him and Winslow?

dialogues.speaker: Matthew
dialogues.text: When I heard about Winslow, I expected at least a few sarcastic remarks from him...

talks.objective: Enter the ruins at the base of the lighthouse

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: N—No... don't come closer... don't come closer... stop flashing...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Oh dear. Winslow.

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: Wh—Who's there! I locked all the doors. How did you get in here!

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: G—Ghosts. P—Please, I apologize. Don't come any closer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... That looks really bad. He's barely making any sense.

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: The white ghost. The white ghost is here...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With a loud scream, the man named Winslow nearly faints on the spot.\nAfter Odolf's comforting words, he finally calms down and regains some of his senses.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Feeling better, Winslow?

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: Better? What do you mean better... Odolf, you... What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: You came to laugh at me, didn't you? And you even brought that white thing with you, just to scare me.

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: You locals. All of you. You've always pushed me away. You're jealous that I live here. You people, you people...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Calm down, Winslow. We're here to help you. We've always been helping you.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: When you were shouting about moving those "damp, horrible, troublesome things" from down below out to the fields beyond the port, we were the ones who stepped in and tried to stop you.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Back then, I told you, "There will be consequences, Winslow." ...It hurts me to see you like this.

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #And then, just these past few days, I returned from Snezhnaya and heard that you were being tormented by some ghosts. So, I immediately brought {NICKNAME} and Paimon here. They can solve this problem.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: We've always been trying to help you, Winslow...

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: Who knows... Who knows if you're doing this on purpose...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #*sigh* Even if you don't trust me, you should at least trust {NICKNAME}. {M#He}{F#She} is an Honorary Knight of the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: That's enough, Winslow. Staying here isn't doing any favors for your sanity.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #Look at this poor fellow! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, I'll take him up above to get some fresh air. We'll leave the ruins to you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If we fail...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then we'll become one of them too...

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: Eeeeeee!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously, there you go, saying creepy things again. Stop scaring people like that!

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Haha. I doubt whatever's down there is that dangerous. Well then, best of luck getting everything sorted out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we definitely will!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Odolf leads the unsteady, pale Winslow away from the ruins beneath the lighthouse...

talks.objective: Disable the alarm mechanism to open the path
Disable the alarm mechanism to open the path

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That alarm was flashing so fast earlier. Paimon really thought there's something dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But now it looks like there's nothing at all. No Abyss monsters, no ghosts either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It almost feels a little lonely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Loneliness is the most frightening thing of all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, is it? Paimon doesn't understand at all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But where did that strong wind just now come from... Wait. It's coming from above.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something just fell from above! Eek!!!

talks.objective: Defeat the Eye of the Storm
Return to the base of the old lighthouse

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Odolf, we're back. How's it going? Any more problems with the alarm?

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: No. It's stopped flashing.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Goodness, that was fast. You two really solved the problem in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. So, about that wind earlier...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: The wind... It must be the cries of fallen knights who refuse to leave this place. The flashing of the alarm was only meant to alert us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehh? Wait, the ghosts are actually...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: The ghosts never meant to harm you, Winslow. They were only upset by the idea of being driven away.

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: R—Really...?

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: They were heroes who gave up their lives fighting the Abyss here. How could they ever wish you harm?

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #Ahem... It's all thanks to {NICKNAME} and Paimon. They are Honorary Knights of the Knights of Favonius and also top-tier... top-tier ghost negotiation experts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Emm... Well, that title does sound kind of cool.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: That loud crash just now. It sounded like the floor split apart. You two weren't hurt, were you...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not a scratch.

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: #That's a relief. I was a little worried just now. Ahem. As for that noise, it was actually... Well, it was {NICKNAME} and Paimon negotiating with the ghosts of the Knights of Favonius through...

dialogues.speaker: Odolf
dialogues.text: Through... a form of super spiritual arm wrestling! Locals all know about it. Ah, it's a perilous method to appease the angry ghosts indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Winslow
dialogues.text: Super spiritual arm wrestling? R—Really?

choices.text: It was just a normal cave-in...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: #Such sheer power! Bringing down ancient ruins during an arm-wrestling match with a ghost? Just another day in the life of the master negotiator {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: In any case, after the negotiation, the ghosts' anger should have settled...

response.speaker: Winslow
response.text: Th—Then they won't come out to cause trouble anymore... No, I mean... they won't come out and mess with the alarm again, right...?

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: It's hard to say, Winslow. It depends on how you behave.

response.speaker: Winslow
response.text: I... I've been on my best behavior these past few days. I cleared the weeds around the heroes' graves and carefully cleaned their tombstones...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: #Goodness! Well done, Winslow. {NICKNAME}'s negotiation went smoothly, and your efforts helped too.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: If you could stay this way forever, the spirits of the fallen would surely rest easy in their graves.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: After all, if they can rest in peace, why would they bother coming back to stir up trouble?

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: #Relax, Winslow. You see, things always work out in the end. And if the alarm malfunctions again, we can always ask {NICKNAME} to come negotiate on your behalf.

response.speaker: Winslow
response.text: *sigh* You're right... Odolf...

response.speaker: Winslow
response.text: My thanks to you as well...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: #All right then. As for {NICKNAME} and Paimon, thank you for what you've done for us. Please take this...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: This is the thing I mentioned preparing earlier. I knew you would be able to resolve this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, it's really a reward. Paimon thought you were preparing some kind of adventuring gear.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: I know my limits. I can handle business well enough, but adventuring is not my strength.

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: All right, my friends. Come by the tavern again sometime. Next time, we can chat about something a little more interesting.

choices.text: A simple flick of the wrist...

response.speaker: Odolf
response.text: #This is something only {NICKNAME} could pull off...
